assertions: Essex shall take Reading: the town will fall to the Parliament army besieging it
The town will be yielded and surrendered on terms/composition, delivered up to Essex, rather than carried by a bloody storm and utter sack

The governor of the town will be unable to hold it: Saturn, lord of the 4th for the governor, in his fall shows his weakness, loss of authority and personal affliction/incapacitation, and the defence collapsing through him

No effective relief from the King will save the town in time: the Sun, the King's significator, in the 7th in a fixed sign shows the King's party standing in opposition and obstinate, but not delivering the town before it is given up

The success will not be immediate or effortless: Mars in his fall, the Moon void of course and her application to Mars counted as a square in signs of long ascension show difficulty, delay and hard going first, then effecting

The town's ammunition and provision are not instantly exhausted: Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus placed therein show store still present, so the surrender comes from the governor's weakness and an untenable defence, not from immediate starvation
Timing is on a day scale, the siege being already in progress: delivery within days, by the end of April, about 27 April
method: Horary astrology per Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II, classical dignities/reception and whole-sign house significators
reasoning: Scorpio ascends, Mars lord of Ascendant = Essex, well fortified save his fall and in mutual reception with Moon in the 10th near Regulus, giving Essex strength and honour; Saturn lord of the 4th (town/governor) in his fall is far weaker, so besieger overcomes besieged. Moon void of course applying to Mars, the sextile equivalent to a square in long ascension, gives difficulty/delay then perfection. Sun King's significator in 7th fixed gives no timely relief. Timing scale: day scale, because question concerns a siege already in progress to be resolved in days; Jupiter/Venus for 5th-house provisions show store present, hence yield on terms rather than famine or storm.
summary: Yes, Essex shall take Reading, the town being delivered up to him on surrender after a hard, delayed siege, through the governor's weakness and failure of relief.
